editions.text:
The day ran busier than the week before at the feeders, with 342 visits against a seven-day average of 308.9, and 20 species against an average of 19.9. Heard detections were quieter, at 393 against an average of 421.7. Tufted Titmouse led the visits with 108 confident sightings, followed by Carolina Chickadee with 45.

Thirteen species were recorded on all seven days, including this one, among them Carolina Wren, Eastern Towhee, Northern Cardinal, and Song Sparrow. Red-shouldered Hawk, recorded on five of the past seven days, was not recorded today, and neither were Brown-headed Cowbird or Pine Siskin. Northern Mockingbird and Red-bellied Woodpecker were both heard today, as they were on six of the seven days.

Eastern Meadowlark, with five confident visual sightings, was recorded at this station for the first time with confidence on this day. No species was heard here for the first time. The audio source was switched repeatedly across the week, and again through this day, so heard counts reflect whichever microphone was active at the time.
